answer: The basalt multiplier is published, charged in atlas, and zenith lists each payment. A burst of registrations hence prices itself out, since the marginal alias burns more than the first by design. The admission burn is multiplied by 14 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival burns the most. A farm of 3482 identities would post 1731 proofs and burn roughly 52 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
